thread:
sophie: :rotating_light: Heads-up — we're seeing a spike in 5xx from hosted inference since the canary rollout at ~10:58. Multiple customers reporting timeouts. Rolling back?
jamal: Confirming. Gateway 504s and API-router 502s up ~12% over baseline in the last 5m. P50 latency unchanged, p95 up. snippet from gateway logs:
```
[2026-03-18T10:59:12Z] auth-proxy:error connection_reset backend=kv-cache host=kv01 code=502
[2026-03-18T10:59:13Z] router:warn busy_queue len=128 drop=4 route=hosted-inference
[2026-03-18T10:59:14Z] svc-inference:timeout model=embedder-v1 rtt=2500ms
```
alex: What did the canary change? I pushed the v2-canary with dense-prefetch turned on (dense-prefetch=true) and bumped prefetch window to 16.
jamal: That dense-prefetch flag increases prefetch lookahead + triggers larger batching. Telemetry shows a big uptick in KV cache misses -> more upstream auth calls and backend churn. Auth-proxy threadpool saturated.
support-bryan: Customer ticket C-8421 (high-QPS hosted customer) just escalated — they see repeated timeouts and billing retries. They want ETA and whether we'll issue credits.
sophie: @oncall-bot rollback-policy canary v2 100%
oncall-bot: rollback initiated for canary v2 -> v1-stable. Notifying infra and starting traffic shift. ETA ~90s.
anna: Before full rollback, can we try flipping the dense-prefetch flag off scoped to the canary? That would be quicker than full service roll. Command: `/feature toggle dense-prefetch --env canary --set false`
jamal: I attempted the feature flip — flag propagation went through but in-flight connections still exhibit new behavior. Looks like we need to drain and restart the canary pool to flush KV cache state. Suggest: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/api-gateway-canary -n inference-canary`
alex: Starting rolling restart now. Also patching prefetch window 16->4 and disabling aggressive batching for the canary hosts.
jamal: After restart: 5xx volume trending back to normal. Saw error rate drop back to baseline within ~90s of node drains. Customer retries are tapering off.
support-bryan: Told customer we've reverted the risky flag and restarted canary. They're asking about billing credits; I'll hold until we confirm full recovery and collect error counts. CC finance if we need to consider credits.
sophie: Notes for postmortem: root cause = dense-prefetch + larger prefetch window under dense production-like traffic causing KV cache miss storm -> auth-proxy saturation -> 502/504s. Mitigations: add preflight canary load test that exercises prefetch and batching; add rollout guard to limit canary traffic slice for config changes; add telemetry alarm for auth-proxy queue depth.
anna: :thumbsup: Let's schedule a blameless postmortem tomorrow 10:00. Owners: jamal (root cause analysis + telemetry), alex (rollout docs + safer defaults), support-bryan (customer comms + billing follow-up).
